transcript.answer:
The `auto-merge` run holds off until four conditions are all true: (1) CI is green; (2) no review thread is open; (3) Lore's review still stands approved on the pull request's current head; (4) the pull request has been open for the minimum age. That age is `auto_merge.min_age_hours`, 24 hours by default. A pull request that is only waiting out its age shows as "merges after …" on the board.

Red CI, a conflict or open review threads don't make the run wait. Those go to the `auto-merge-fix` agent, for at most three rounds. Per PR #3320, a pull request is parked, not approved, in two cases: Lore's own pull request when no lore-reviewer App is installed, because GitHub refuses an approval from the PR's author; and a failed run or a reason only a person can clear.

A later change, #1731e90, says `auto-merge-fix` no longer merges the base in or edits other authors' branches. It says auto merge only waits and approves. The implementation loop keeps its own pull request mergeable instead. I did not open that commit in full, so the details of that change are unconfirmed.

PR #3433 says open review threads are what keep the loop off a pull request with unaddressed findings, and that an approving re-check no longer resolves Lore's earlier threads.

judgements.reason: The answer states that red CI, a conflict or open review threads don't make the run wait, which the gold answer contradicts; it also leaves merge conflicts out of its list of wait conditions.
